hook.text: Dick's Bar in New York was where Merritt wrote much of its 69 love songs, and he said he spent eight hours a day there.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: April 1999 at Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics

sentences.text: In the first plan, four drag queens would star in a theatre revue, and the one the crowd liked most by the end of the evening would be paid.
In a gay piano bar in Manhattan, Merritt heard a pianist play Stephen Sondheim songs and decided to move into theatre music.
He began with one hundred love songs, a way of introducing himself to the world.
Working out how long that would take, he settled on sixty-nine.
He had read about Charles Ives's 114 Songs that day and thought he could do something similar.
Fleetwood Mac, Billie Holiday and Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark were other influences.
He also produced and engineered the record, with five other people on engineering and Jeff Lipton on mastering.
Recording happened in April 1999 at four studios: Polar West, Mother West, Polar Mother and Sonics.
Shirley Simms sang on several songs, and Dudley Klute took lead vocals on six.
Sam Davol played cello and flute, and Daniel Handler added accordion and keyboards.
In May 2000 Circus released it in Europe and Australia, without the booklet.
In April 2010 Merge issued a limited vinyl edition of 1,000 copies.
In December 2006 LD Beghtol published a book on the album in Continuum's 33 1/3 series.
The band played all 69 songs in order seven times, five in America and two in London.
Peter Gabriel covered "The Book of Love", and Superchunk covered "I Don't Want to Get Over You" in 2025.
